analysis: In the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), prostacyclin analogues are commonly used to help dilate blood vessels and improve blood flow. Iloprost, Treprostinil, and Epoprostenol are all known to be analogues of prostacyclin, which is a well-established fact in medical literature. Riociguat, on the other hand, functions through a different mechanism as a soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator, which helps to increase the levels of cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) leading to vasodilation. This mechanism is distinct from that of prostacyclin analogues. Therefore, based on standard medical knowledge and consensus, Riociguat is the drug that is NOT an analogue of prostacyclin.
